search_log: Searched “Everything's Eventual point of view first person third person” and opened the Internet Writing Workshop discussion and BookRags study guide.
Opened the Simon & Schuster publisher page and verified its sustained first-person excerpt from “Autopsy Room Four.”
Opened The New Yorker’s authorized texts of “All That You Love Will Be Carried Away” and “The Man in the Black Suit,” confirming sustained third- and first-person stories respectively.
Opened StephenKing.com and verified that the differently narrated works are separate constituent stories in the fourteen-story collection.

Searched Google Books and Open Library previews for a single authorized whole-book source exposing both persons; the accessible pages verified the contents but did not provide sufficient mixed-person prose.
Searched academic-domain and PDF results for a scholarly whole-collection POV analysis; no Tier B source explicitly establishing the collection-wide alternation was found.
person_note: The volume contains autonomous stories with different controlling persons. The quote sample exposes first-person narration in the title story and other tales, while q00821 belongs to an authorized sustained third-person story. Publisher and New Yorker texts independently establish full first- and third-person constituent narratives, so the difference is structural rather than isolated dialogue, thought, or embedded material. The book is therefore ALTERNATING. Confidence is medium because the Tier A sources establish the component persons only at named-story scope; the sources explicitly describing the whole collection as mixed-person are Tier C, so the evidence does not meet the methodology’s threshold for high confidence.
